description: Team Freefall is a collaborative team participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We aim to explore NASA's microgravity combustion research and develop an AI-powered dashboard that makes scientific findings easier to understand, compare, and explore. Through research, data analysis, and innovative technology, we hope to generate meaningful insights into fire safety for future human space missions.
summary:
To whom it may concern, greetings!

Our project is called FlameGuard AI. It uses AI and NASA's available PSI databases to rank and prioritise relevant NASA research from over the years.

We understand that during launches and other situations, such as training, certain safety measures can sometimes be overlooked. But what if a fire breaks out unexpectedly? We wouldn't necessarily know what to do, especially if the fire were aboard the ISS or any other kind of spacecraft or satellite, because fire behaves differently on Earth and in space, particularly in microgravity.

To better understand this behaviour and make relevant research more accessible, my team and I have created a dashboard that showcases relevant research for researchers and curious individuals to explore. Moreover, it also has a graph that can visualise how a flame might behave under certain conditions, depending on factors such as the type of fuel, the availability of oxygen, and even the amount of gravity.

Safe to say, this dashboard can quench the thirst of curious scientists while also making existing scientific research more accessible and useful for understanding fire safety in space.
details:
FlameGuard AI is a dashboard that ranks the relevance of various research papers, literature, and databases provided by NASA and external agencies.

My team and I developed it using multiple AI engines, such as ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude, to help us translate our ideas and expectations into code. We then uploaded our project to GitHub and integrated it with Streamlit, making it publicly accessible.

FlameGuard AI has various functions apart from simply ranking research. It compares different research articles, literature, and projects to identify and highlight the most relevant ones. Apart from that, it also features a graph that can simulate flame behaviour under different conditions, including variations in airflow and oxygen availability during combustion in microgravity.

Along with this, it has the PSI Co-Pilot, an AI-powered feature that ranks different research investigations according to the questions you provide. You can then explore these research articles and literature further through whichever website or web browser you prefer.

We purposefully designed FlameGuard AI to have a distinct visual identity. The dashboard is primarily black, with white text and red and yellow accents. We chose this combination to make it look professional while also catching the user's eye. It gives off a certain feeling of rawness, you know, like how a hacker feels when they see their own code, or how a biologist feels when they observe a particular organism growing in a culture. It gives you the feeling that you're creating something on your own, which is certainly super satisfying.

We didn't just copy and paste whatever the AI suggested. We tried to develop new ideas, integrate them, and add features beyond what our original problem statement asked of us.

FlameGuard AI is not just about meticulously reading literature, but rather understanding how fire can harm, fascinate, and continuously intrigue our curious minds.

When we simulate a flame on our graph, we get curiouser and curiouser. When we ask questions through the PSI Co-Pilot, we often find ourselves falling into a research rabbit hole.

And at the end of this amazing journey, we're left rejuvenated with knowledge, exhausted because we certainly did stare at our screens for far too long, and satisfied that we did something well worth our time.

Thank you.
